title: Hiring at a Fair Rate
statement:
A company wants to hire exactly `k` of `n` workers. Worker `i` has quality `q_i` and asks for at least `w_i` money. The pay must be fair: every hired worker is paid in proportion to quality, so the pay of worker `i` is `r * q_i` for one common rate `r` (which need not be an integer). Each hired worker must get at least what they ask, so `r * q_i >= w_i` for all hired workers.

Choose the `k` workers and the rate to make the total pay as small as possible. The total `r * (sum of q_i)` may be fractional; print it rounded up to the next integer.

## Input
The first line contains `n` and `k`. Each of the next `n` lines contains `q_i` and `w_i`.

## Output
Print the smallest possible total pay, rounded up to an integer.

## Constraints
- `1 <= k <= n <= 11000`
- `1 <= q_i, w_i <= 10^6`
